general_concept_gap.title: General Concept Gap
general_concept_gap.explanation: Some of your answers suggest gaps in the core ideas for this topic. Revisit the key definitions, diagrams, and example questions before trying a new quiz.
general_concept_gap.focus_area: Review the main definitions and standard diagrams in your textbook for this topic.

first_law_reflection_angle.title: Angle of Incidence and Reflection
first_law_reflection_angle.explanation: Angle of incidence equals angle of reflection (i = r). Both angles are always measured from the NORMAL to the surface, not from the mirror surface itself.
first_law_reflection_angle.focus_area: Highlight the normal line at the point of incidence and mark equal angles i and r on either side of the normal.

second_law_reflection_plane.title: Rays in the Same Plane
second_law_reflection_plane.explanation: According to the second law of reflection, the incident ray, reflected ray and the normal at the point of incidence all lie in the same plane.
second_law_reflection_plane.focus_area: Show the incident ray, reflected ray and the normal drawn on a single flat surface to emphasize they are coplanar.

plane_mirror_image_properties.title: Plane Mirror Image Properties
plane_mirror_image_properties.explanation: A plane mirror forms a virtual, erect image of the same size as the object, placed as far behind the mirror as the object is in front. The image is laterally inverted.
plane_mirror_image_properties.focus_area: Highlight object and image distances from the mirror and show lateral inversion (left-right reversal).

refraction_bending_normal.title: Bending Towards or Away from Normal
refraction_bending_normal.explanation: When light travels from a rarer medium (like air) to a denser medium (like glass), it bends towards the normal. When it travels from a denser to a rarer medium, it bends away from the normal.
refraction_bending_normal.focus_area: Show incident and refracted rays on both sides of the boundary and emphasize how their direction changes relative to the normal.

angle_from_surface.title: Angles Measured from Surface
angle_from_surface.explanation: Angle of incidence and angle of reflection are never measured from the mirror surface itself. Both angles are always measured from the NORMAL drawn perpendicular to the mirror.
angle_from_surface.focus_area: Draw the normal as a perpendicular line to the mirror and shade the angles between the rays and this normal, not the mirror surface.

reflection_not_equal.title: i and r Must Be Equal
reflection_not_equal.explanation: According to the first law of reflection, the angle of incidence is exactly equal to the angle of reflection (i = r) when light reflects from a smooth surface.
reflection_not_equal.focus_area: Show incident and reflected rays making equal angles with the normal, and explicitly label i and r as equal.

normal_orientation_wrong.title: Normal Drawn Incorrectly
normal_orientation_wrong.explanation: The normal is an imaginary line drawn perpendicular to the mirror surface at the point where the ray hits, not parallel or at any random angle.
normal_orientation_wrong.focus_area: Highlight the mirror surface and then draw the normal at 90° to it exactly at the point of incidence.

plane_not_same.title: Rays Not in Same Plane
plane_not_same.explanation: The incident ray, reflected ray and the normal at the point of incidence must all lie in the same plane. If you draw them in different planes, the second law of reflection is violated.
plane_not_same.focus_area: Show the mirror, normal and both rays drawn together on a single flat surface to emphasize they are coplanar.
